newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: UAE group raises highest bid for former BCCI unit.
newsitem.headline: UAE group raises highest bid for former BCCI unit.

text.p: A consortium led by a businessman from the United Arab Emirates lodged the highest bid for Pakistan's Habib Credit and Exchange Bank Ltd (HCEBL) on Thursday and later raised it further, the state Privatisation Commission said.

Sheikh Nahayan bin Mubarak Al Nayahan first bid 38 rupees per share for the 42 million shares, representing a 70 percent equity stake in HCEBL, which was once part of the collapsed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI).
But the commission, in later talks, succeeded in getting the bid price revised to 39 rupees per share, a commission statement said.
A commission meeting recommended to submit the bid to a cabinet committee on privatisation for a decision at its meeting due on Saturday, it said.

The only other bidder to show up out of nine foreign and local companies that had shown interest in HCEBL was the Fauji Foundation, a private business group run partly as a welfare foundation for retired Pakistani army personnel.
Fauji Foundation's final bid was 37.60 rupees.
The government will retain 20 percent of HCEBL's shares and 10 percent will be offered to its employees.
HCEBL net profit rose five percent in the year ended December 31, over its 1995 profit of 265 million rupees.

HCEBL, formed in 1992 as a subsidiary of the state-owned Habib Bank Limited from three BCCI branches in Pakistan, is the third Pakistani bank to be privatised after Muslim Commercial Bank and Allied Bank Ltd.

It was the first time since Pakistan launched its privatisation programme in 1991 that bidding had been shown live on television in what commission said was an attempt to demonstrate that the proceedings were transparent and above board.
